headline: Debutants Cape Verde reach World Cup round of 32 after draw with Saudi Arabia
summary: The historic achievement for the debutants comes as Spain tops Group H, while Uruguay and Saudi Arabia are eliminated from the tournament.
details: Debutants Cape Verde have secured a historic place in the World Cup round of 32 after playing to a 0-0 draw with Saudi Arabia in Houston on Friday.
The result ensures Cape Verde advances as Group H runners-up, continuing a journey that has captured the imagination of football fans worldwide.
Spain earned the top spot in the pool with seven points following a 1-0 victory over Uruguay, with a decisive strike from Baena.
Uruguay and Saudi Arabia were both eliminated from the tournament, finishing with two points each.
In the match between Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia, Cape Verde looked the more likely to score but lacked composure in the final third.
A key chance for Cape Verde was saved by Saudi Arabian goalkeeper Mohammed Alowais after Laros Duarte missed a one-on-one opportunity.
Saudi Arabia exited the tournament meekly, having scored only a single goal in their three group stage matches.
Cape Verde will now face Argentina in the next stage of the competition.
caption:
From debutants to history-makers! Cape Verde reaches the World Cup round of 32.

Debutants Cape Verde have secured a historic place in the World Cup round of 32 after playing to a 0-0 draw with Saudi Arabia in Houston on Friday.

The result ensures Cape Verde advances as Group H runners-up, continuing a journey that has captured the imagination of football fans worldwide.

Spain earned the top spot in the pool with seven points following a 1-0 victory over Uruguay, with a decisive strike from Baena.

Uruguay and Saudi Arabia were both eliminated from the tournament, finishing with two points each.

In the match between Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia, Cape Verde looked the more likely to score but lacked composure in the final third.

A key chance for Cape Verde was saved by Saudi Arabian goalkeeper Mohammed Alowais after Laros Duarte missed a one-on-one opportunity.

Saudi Arabia exited the tournament meekly, having scored only a single goal in their three group stage matches.

Cape Verde will now face Argentina in the next stage of the competition.

headline_marked: 920 dead, 50,000 missing after [[twin earthquakes strike Venezuela]]
headline: 920 dead, 50,000 missing after twin earthquakes strike Venezuela
summary: Two powerful quakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 flattened buildings in the north, leaving tens of thousands trapped under rubble.
details: Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck northern Venezuela on Wednesday evening, killing at least 920 people. According to the UN, more than 50,000 people are still missing as rescue efforts continue.
The coastal area of La Guaira, near the capital Caracas, was the worst hit. Entire residential complexes were reduced to rubble, with rescue teams reporting total collapse in several areas.

International aid is pouring in, with search and rescue teams from 17 countries, including Chile, Spain, and Mexico, now on the ground. The US is sending a disaster response team of over 250 personnel and specialized search dogs.

Local residents have expressed fury over the perceived lack of official response. Many were seen using their bare hands to dig for survivors while jeering government officials during visits to devastated neighborhoods.
The disaster strikes a country already crippled by over a decade of economic collapse, which has hollowed out public services and hospitals. This is Venezuela's most powerful earthquake since 1900.

Foreign casualties include nine Portuguese nationals, five Spaniards, two Brazilians, two Chinese nationals, and one Italian-Venezuelan. Over 180 Portuguese and Spanish citizens remain unaccounted for.
caption:
920 dead and 50,000 missing. Venezuela is facing its worst earthquake in over a century.

Twin earthquakes of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 struck northern Venezuela on Wednesday evening, killing at least 920 people. According to the UN, more than 50,000 people are still missing as rescue efforts continue.

The coastal area of La Guaira, near the capital Caracas, was the worst hit. Entire residential complexes were reduced to rubble, with rescue teams reporting total collapse in several areas.

International aid is pouring in, with search and rescue teams from 17 countries, including Chile, Spain, and Mexico, now on the ground. The US is sending a disaster response team of over 250 personnel and specialized search dogs.

Local residents have expressed fury over the perceived lack of official response. Many were seen using their bare hands to dig for survivors while jeering government officials during visits to devastated neighborhoods.

The disaster strikes a country already crippled by over a decade of economic collapse, which has hollowed out public services and hospitals. This is Venezuela's most powerful earthquake since 1900.

Foreign casualties include nine Portuguese nationals, five Spaniards, two Brazilians, two Chinese nationals, and one Italian-Venezuelan. Over 180 Portuguese and Spanish citizens remain unaccounted for.
